preview_strategy_trade_levels.description: Before committing a stop, target or R:R change, see what the strategy's trade-level menu builds on one coin right now, both directions: every stop × exit-plan pair that survives with each target's price and close %, stop distance in %, the plan's R:R measured from that pair's own stop, and a runner's trail distance in ATR and R; every stop option, each with the verdict its row describes, the bound that refused it and the ATR multiple it was judged at (an ATR option's own multiple; bounds are inclusive) — the one statement of a stop's distance in ATR; refused target options; refused pairs, each with the reason its row describes and the ratio it reached, stated to 3 decimals; and the reachable stop band in ATR and %. Every price is on the venue's price grid, rounded once the way its order rests — a stop toward entry, a target away from it, a resting entry away from the mark. Each pair's stop and target distances and the entry's distance from the mark are measured between those grid prices and stated to 4 decimals; a stop row's distance is its option's own figure. Each direction's `entry` is null for an at-market entry; under a level trigger it states the entry on the direction's construction basis — the level read, the placed price, its side of the mark and the order that RESTS there (the construction is built at that placed price), with how far it sits from the mark (distancePct, distanceAtr) and how long it stays valid (validForMinutes), or why it is refused (WRONG_SIDE with the side the order needed, LEVEL_UNREAD, ATR_UNAVAILABLE). `source` is the player's staged draft ({"kind":"DRAFT", strategyId, draftVersion} at the draftVersion get_strategy_draft returned, composed as commit_strategy_draft would compose it — a moved draft is refused with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED) or a committed strategy ({"kind":"COMMITTED", strategyId}). The same computation as the Strategy Studio's preview; writes nothing.

direction.description: The direction this preview is for; key on it, not on position.

minRiskRewardRatio.description: Judged per pair on the exit plan's risk-reward; an all-R plan below it is refused when the strategy is saved.

mark.description: The live mark the placed price is judged against.

levelPrice.description: The entry level read on the decided bar.

placedPrice.description: The price the order rests at; the construction is built from it.

orderType.description: The order that rests: TRIGGER (stop) or LIMIT.

distancePct.description: The distance of the placed price from the mark, in percent of the mark.

validForMinutes.description: The maximum age a position decided now would be minted with, in minutes: how long the order may rest unfilled.

requiredSide.description: The side the order needed; null under EITHER_SIDE_OF_LEVEL.

entry.description: The level entry on this direction's construction basis — where the order rests, or why it is refused; null for an at-market entry.

anyOf.description: The coin's ATR could not be read: no construction.

stage.description: `LEVEL_UNREAD`: The entry level has no reading on this bar, so no order can be placed and nothing is built. `WRONG_SIDE`: The entry order would sit on the side of price it cannot rest on, so nothing is built for this side.

edge.description: The level's reading; null when it had none.

placed.description: Where the order would have rested; null when the level was unread.

anyOf.description: The strategy's entry level refused for this direction: no construction, and the trade is not offered.

entryPrice.description: The entry anchor every distance is measured from: the judged live mark.

atrPct.description: That ATR as a percent of the entry anchor.

hardStopDistancePct.description: The Hard stop distance on this coin, percent of entry.

price.description: The stop price; null only when its level had no reading.

atrMultiple.description: The ATR option's AUTHORED multiple; null for a level or percent stop.

distancePct.description: Distance from entry, percent of entry.

distanceAtrMultiple.description: The distance the bounds judged, in ATR multiples: an ATR option's own authored multiple, any other stop's distance measured once in ATR. Bounds are inclusive — a stop authored on one survives.

levelReading.description: The reading a LEVEL stop was built from: for a nearest level, its pick among the candidates on the loss side of the entry; on a WRONG_SIDE row, the level's own reading. Null for an ATR or PERCENT stop and on LEVEL_UNREAD.

verdict.description: `SURVIVED`: Inside your band — this stop can be paired with a target. `BELOW_FLOOR` (`minStopLossAtrMultiple`): Closer to entry than your floor allows on this coin. Lower the floor to keep it. `ABOVE_CEILING` (`maxStopLossAtrMultiple`): Further from entry than your hard stop allows. Widening the hard stop keeps it — and moves the resting order out with it, which buys a smaller position for the same risk budget. `ABOVE_STRUCTURAL_CEILING`: Past the platform cap of 5 × ATR, which applies at every setting — no dial recovers it. `LEVEL_UNREAD`: The level has no reading on this bar, so this stop has no price here. It is never substituted or stretched. `WRONG_SIDE`: This stop sits on the profit side of entry on this bar, so it cannot protect the trade. A nearest level — a zone edge or midpoint, a pool, a naked POC or a single print — looks past its own pick to the next of its kind on the loss side, and is refused only when none sits there, at its own reading. A refused stop makes no pair with any target.

responsibleBound.description: The configured dial that refused it; null otherwise.

rejectedByThresholdPct.description: The bound that refused it — the min stop, the Hard stop or the structural cap, as a multiple times the ATR percent — in percent of entry.

stopCandidates.description: Every stop option with its verdict, tightest first.

rewardToHardStopRatio.description: The plan's share-weighted reward distance ÷ the Hard stop distance.

runnerTrail.description: The runner's trail distance on this bar, in ATR and in R; null when the plan closes 100%.

items.description: A surviving stop × exit-plan pair. Every target is priced beside THIS pair's stop (an R target sits multiple × |entry − this stop| from entry); riskRewardRatio is the plan's: each share at its target, the runner at the last target that closes a share, a 0% trail objective at nothing.

reason.description: `TARGETS_OUT_OF_ORDER`: The plan’s targets do not run away from entry in plan order. `RISK_REWARD_TOO_LOW` (`minRiskRewardRatio`): The plan pays less than your min R:R. Lower it to keep the plan. `TARGET_LEG_BELOW_ORDER_FLOOR`: A target’s share of the smallest order this agent can place is under the exchange minimum.

computedRR.description: The plan's share-weighted risk-reward beside this stop, stated to 3 decimals.

rejectedPairs.description: The refused stop × exit-plan pairs, each with its reason and the ratio it attained. TARGET_LEG_BELOW_ORDER_FLOOR never appears here: the preview binds no agent, so no order floor applies.

price.description: The target's price; on WRONG_SIDE, the level's own reading; null on LEVEL_UNREAD.

stage.description: `LEVEL_UNREAD`: The level has no reading on this bar, so this target has no price here. `WRONG_SIDE`: This level sits on the loss side of entry on this bar, so it cannot be a target. A nearest level looks past its own pick to the next of its kind beyond the entry, and is refused only when none sits there, at its own reading. It makes no pair.

reachableMinPct.description: The deterministic 1×ATR distance, percent of entry.

reachableMaxPct.description: The structural 5×ATR cap, percent of entry.

requestedMinAtrMultiple.description: The min stop as configured, in ATR.

requestedMinPct.description: The min stop resolved on this coin, percent of entry.

requestedMaxAtrMultiple.description: The Hard stop as configured, in ATR.

requestedMaxPct.description: The Hard stop ceiling resolved on this coin, percent of entry: the threshold a stop is judged against.

previews.description: One per direction, LONG then SHORT.

discard_strategy_draft.description: Destroy the player's draft of one strategy at the draftVersion get_strategy_draft returned. It is the PLAYER's decision, never your judgement that a draft looks stale: tell them when it was last written and by which surface, and discard only on their word. It touches no strategy, no revision and no other draft, and it cannot be undone. Refused with DRAFT_VERSION_MOVED when the draft changed after your read, so a write that landed since is never destroyed.

get_metric_construction_hints.description: Get the canonical native value contract and executable transform-authoring hints for one metric returned by list_strategy_vocabulary.

list_strategy_vocabulary.description: List compact report-authoring vocabulary for one category, for a search, or for a search within one category, including metrics, transforms, timeframe references, budgets, enabled timeframes, and template summaries — the platform's templates, then the player's own saved sections as `kind: "saved"` (the live library, which `vocabularyDigest` does not cover). `query` (such as "rsi", "support" or "volume spike") returns the metrics whose key, name, description or family contain every word of it, across every family unless `category` is named; name at least one of the two. This is where a metric key is found: input schemas name a metric as a plain key and refuse one the catalog lacks. Also returns `scalarFamilies` — every report-level scalar operand with its gloss, legal condition operators and label vocabulary, one entry per metric with its scopes named against it. That set is category-independent and is what preview_strategy_report references by `vocabularyDigest` instead of restating.

category.description: One canonical metric family returned by list_strategy_categories.

query.description: Words a metric's key, name, description or family must all contain, such as "volume spike".

list_strategy_categories.description: Start here for report work, authoring or analysis. Returns (a) `modules` — every platform report section with its display name, description, bullet points, and the `moduleName` the market-context tools accept for the same section — and (b) `categories`, the canonical metric categories with authoring guidance and examples. To READ the market: pass a section straight to preview_strategy_report as {"kind":"platform","sectionKey":"includeRsi"}; no other vocabulary is needed. To AUTHOR a column: pass one returned category to list_strategy_vocabulary.

get_strategy_section_template.description: Get the full canonical definition for one platform, custom or saved report template listed by list_strategy_vocabulary. A custom template and a player's saved section ({"kind":"saved","savedSectionId":…}) are copy sources: place their columns — and a saved section's title, note and subject (`benchmarkTicker`, `marketScope`) — in a new custom section of the draft; nothing links back.

list_strategies.description: List the visible SYSTEM catalog and owned PRIVATE strategies with revision, lifecycle, usage, and quota summaries, plus each strategy's card projection (ladder rungs, condition and exit tallies, entry trigger, reward-to-risk floor, hard stop) and your own agents, open positions and all-time results on it. Include inactive owned strategies when looking for one to restore.

forkedFromStrategyName.description: The fork source's name when it is a SYSTEM strategy, the caller's own or one currently published; null when the strategy is not a fork, or when its source is none of those.

save_report_section.description: Save one custom report section to the player's saved-section library, for reuse in any strategy. `section` is a custom section's content — title, notes, its subject and columns. The subject is `benchmarkTicker` (a coin, or a declared stablecoin pair such as USDT_USD) or `marketScope` (the market at one breadth scope), at most one set and both null for the coin under evaluation: a section from a staged draft or a committed strategy is saved by dropping its `kind` and `sectionKey`. The library is keyed by title: a title the player already saved is REPLACED whole (its note, subject and columns), keeping its savedSectionId, and the result says `replaced: true`; `replaced` describes this call, so repeating a save that already landed answers true. Call it only on the player's confirmed word, and before saving a title list_strategy_vocabulary already lists as `kind: "saved"`, tell them it will be replaced. The section is judged as a section that stands alone, with the codes a strategy save returns; a refusal's `path` addresses it as `sections[0]` of a one-section report. Report-level budgets are judged when the section joins a strategy. Refused FORBIDDEN when the save would add a section past the player's library limit; a replace is admitted at the limit. Saved sections are listed by list_strategy_vocabulary and read whole by get_strategy_section_template.

remove_saved_report_section.description: Remove one of the player's saved report sections by its savedSectionId (from list_strategy_vocabulary's `kind: "saved"` templates). The library entry is gone with no other copy; sections already copied into strategies are untouched. An id the player does not hold changes nothing and is answered the same. Call it only on the player's confirmed word, after telling them what it removes.
